europe.rationale: Facts: euro area flash HICP was 4.0% in October (energy +20.8%, core 2.5%). The ECB held the deposit rate at 2.50% on 29 Oct but signalled December is live, and the euro AAA 2y (2.96%) prices about two more hikes. The BoE hiked 8-1 to 4.0% on 5 Nov. On the positive side, the STOXX 600 ended the week only about 0.2% lower against a 5.5% one-day Nasdaq drop, ASML fell only about 1%, and TTF gas and Brent fell sharply on US-Iran deal hopes, which pulled the AAA 10y down to 3.29% from 3.50%. Interpretation: Europe's low AI weight and the energy relief offset hawkish ECB/BoE risk, wider euro sovereign/credit spreads (all-bonds vs AAA 10y about 60bp, up from about 43bp) and defence weakness (Rheinmetall profit warning). Net neutral, and the energy relief reverses if the Iran talks fail.

developed_ex_us.rationale: Facts: the components point different ways. Europe (about half the bucket) is neutral. Japan, the largest single-country weight, entered a bear market (Nikkei -5.96% on 6 Nov and more than -9% on the week, led by SoftBank, Advantest, Tokyo Electron and Kioxia), but Topix rose on 5 Nov and fell less overall. Canada and Australia were roughly flat to slightly positive: TSX +0.5% for the week while the ASX 200 fell 0.5% on 6 Nov. Central banks outside the US are tightening into slowing growth: BoE to 4.0%, RBA to 4.85% (6-3), BoC to 2.5% with Canadian unemployment at 6.7%. AUD (-1.6%) and CAD (-0.9%) fell on 6 Nov. Interpretation: the low AI weight cushions the bucket, but the Japan/Korea AI-hardware legs and synchronised hikes tilt risk slightly down. A weighted net of about -0.3 rounds to 0, so watch SOX and the Nov 10 TSMC/SoftBank prints.

asia_dev_other.rationale: Facts: on 6 Nov the KOSPI fell 6.02% to 5,059.69 after a Level-1 circuit breaker, with foreigners net selling about 12tn won over six sessions (concentrated in SK hynix) and USD/KRW at 1,356.6. Taiwan's TAIEX fell 4.51% (-12.19% on the week, a bear market), prompting a NT$500bn stabilisation-fund authorisation and short-sale curbs from 9 Nov. Korea's only concrete step so far is a 3-month margin-collateral waiver, with no stabilisation fund or short ban. The RBA's fifth hike (4.85%) and DBS/UOB Q3 misses weigh on Australia and Singapore. Interpretation: this is a US policy and financing shock to AI hardware, not a demand collapse. October Korean chip exports were +259% y/y, TSMC guided Q4 to about +14% q/q, and a policy backstop is forming, so it is -1 rather than -2. Chip exports peaked in September, and the TSMC October sales print (about 10 Nov) is the swing factor.

regime_notes: One AI-buildout shock (the US midterm data-centre backlash plus the Microsoft/Oracle/neocloud pullback, SOX -12% on 5 Nov) spread to Korea, Taiwan and Japan on 6 Nov. Europe, Canada and Australia were largely bystanders because of their low AI weight. Hard AI demand data (Korean chip exports +259%, TSMC Q4 guide) contradicts a demand collapse, so the Asian developed markets get -1, not -2, and the score can mean-revert with SOX. The second driver is the Iran war-premium unwind: Brent and TTF fell sharply, which relieves Europe's energy-led inflation (HICP 4.0%), but it depends on diplomacy and would reverse on a US strike decision. Central banks outside the US are hiking into slowing growth (BoE 4.0%, RBA 4.85%, BoC 2.5%, ECB December live), a headwind for rate-sensitive sectors and housing. Nov 9-10 is the key window: Taiwan short curbs and the Korea margin waiver start on 9 Nov, the EWY/EWS index switch happens on 9 Nov, and TSMC October sales, SoftBank results and US CPI land on 10 Nov.

red_flags.issue: Index change: iShares moves EWY (Korea) and EWS (Singapore) to MSCI 25/50 Daily 25 Capped indexes on or around 9 Nov, trimming any group entity above 25% back to 22.5% between rebalances. Expect mechanical trims to the Samsung group and some tracking difference against older benchmarks.
Index change: EWG (Germany) moves to an MSCI 25/50 index on or around 1 Dec 2026, per the same iShares supplement.

Market-structure change: from 9 Nov Taiwan caps intraday short sales of borrowed shares at 3% of the 30-day average daily volume (from 30%) and raises the short-sale margin to 130%. The stabilisation fund is authorised to buy. This can distort hedging and creation/redemption costs and cause NAV/price gaps.

Korea is at a Level-1 circuit breaker (the 11th of 2026) and the US-listed ETF priced the move a day before the home market (EWY -13.46% on 5 Nov). EWY was at -0.09% to NAV on 6 Nov, so there is no discount now, but expect large overnight timing gaps.
Holding-level: Rheinmetall, a top weight, cut its 2026 guidance for the second time and fell more than 17% on 5 Nov. Check each fund's concentration.
